A_target.statement:
Let $f: \R^n \to \R$ be [[Definition:Differentiable Mapping|differentiable]] with a [[Definition:Local Minimum|local minimum]] at $x^*$.
Then:
:$\nabla \map f {x^*} = \mathbf 0$

B_source.statement:
Let $g: \R \to \R$ be [[Definition:Differentiable Real Function|differentiable]] with an [[Definition:Local Extremum|extremum]] at an interior point $t^*$.
Then:
:$\map {g'} {t^*} = 0$

substitutions.the derivative f'(x*): each partial derivative / the gradient grad f(x*)
substitutions.one-variable perturbation x* + h: perturbation along each coordinate direction e_i

derived.f'(x*) = 0: partial f / partial x_i (x*) = 0 for every i

object_map.reformulation: Apply the one-variable stationarity condition along each coordinate direction; the collection of conditions is the vanishing gradient.

validity_conditions: Restricting f to the line x* + t e_i gives a one-variable function with an interior extremum at t=0.
One-variable Fermat gives d/dt f(x* + t e_i)|_0 = partial f/partial x_i (x*) = 0.
Holding for every i means grad f(x*) = 0; extending from 1 to n variables is genuine generalization.
proof_plan: Fix a coordinate direction $e_i$ and let $\map g t = \map f {x^* + t e_i}$.

$g$ has an interior extremum at $t = 0$.
By [[Derivative at Maximum or Minimum]]:
:$\map {g'} 0 = 0$

By the [[Chain Rule for Derivatives|chain rule]]:
:$\map {g'} 0 = \dfrac {\partial f} {\partial x_i} \paren {x^*}$
